first_impression.reaction: Googled 'wedding flowers in season' on the train. Title says 'by Month', so I expected a list of flowers per month. The intro is short and the Key Takeaways are clean, but none of them names a single flower. I scrolled to my month hoping for names and got questions to ask a florist instead. Useful-ish, but not what I searched for. Might bookmark for the florist questions, wouldn't enquire.

journey.quote: Choosing wedding flowers in season starts with a date, not a mood board.
journey.reaction: Nice opening line, quick to read. But I still don't know what's in season.

journey.quote: This guide follows the Australian year, season by season and month by month, with the questions worth putting to your florist for each one.
journey.reaction: Wait, questions? I wanted flowers. This is where I realise the page won't actually list them, and it should just say that straight away and say why.

journey.quote: Australian summer is December, January and February, winter is June, July and August, and the northern tropics run on a wet and dry season instead.
journey.reaction: Clear and handy since I'm used to the opposite. Fine, but it's about seasons, not flowers.

journey.section: Wedding flowers in season in Australia by month
journey.quote: What grows well in a given month varies with the region, the grower and the year, so the month notes below are about the conversation rather than a fixed list.
journey.reaction: Okay, at least it's honest. But this is the real answer to my search and it's buried halfway down. If I'd known from the top I'd have gone straight to the month links.

journey.section: Summer in December, January and February
journey.quote: Ask how close to the ceremony the florist can set up, so arrangements spend as little time as possible in warm air.
journey.reaction: Practical tip, I'd actually use this. But it's a paragraph of questions per month on a phone, a lot of scrolling.

journey.section: Summer in December, January and February
journey.quote: Our notes on [December](/8-in-season-flowers-for-december) flowers go into more detail.
journey.reaction: This link is what I actually want. I'd tap it. Pity only some months have one.

journey.section: Spring in September, October and November
journey.quote: Waratah flowering is concentrated in spring, and growers have worked to stretch its season to reach peak demand periods such as Christmas.
journey.reaction: Finally a real flower name, with a source. This is the most search-matching line on the page and it's way down.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, the [Department of Agriculture's import conditions](https://www.agriculture.gov.au/biosecurity-trade/policy/risk-analysis/memos/ba2018-12) require importers to manage biosecurity risk before they send cut flowers and foliage to Australia.
journey.reaction: Dated and linked to the government. Tells me it's current. Good.

journey.quote: - **What is the backup?** If an imported or late stem is not available, what goes in its place, and in what colour and shape.
journey.reaction: The three questions list is screenshot-worthy. Short and scannable.

journey.section: Planning your flowers and spend with your florist
journey.quote: Season and sourcing both affect the cost of a design.
journey.reaction: Just tell me how much it costs. At least it links to a cost guide, so I'd click that next.

journey.quote: ### Which flower is in season in Australian spring?
journey.reaction: Exactly the kind of question I'd type, short direct answer. More of these would make the page.

turn_offs_found.quote: Wedding Flowers in Season in Australia by Month
turn_offs_found.why: The title promises flowers by month, but the month sections are questions for a florist with almost no flower names. Heading doesn't match what I get.

turn_offs_found.quote: What grows well in a given month varies with the region, the grower and the year, so the month notes below are about the conversation rather than a fixed list.
turn_offs_found.why: The honest explanation is fine, but it should be in the first 100 words, not halfway down after I've already scrolled hunting for a list.

turn_offs_found.quote: Waratah flowering is concentrated in spring, and growers have worked to stretch its season to reach peak demand periods such as Christmas.
turn_offs_found.why: The only concrete, sourced flower answer is below three seasons of month notes. It belongs in Key Takeaways.

would_share_with: My fiancé: a screenshot of the three questions (What is local? What is imported? What is the backup?)

cta_reaction.why: I came for a flower list, don't know the brand, and nothing tells me what it costs or whether it's for someone outside Australia. I'd tap the month and cost guide links, not this.

top_3_changes: Say up front that this is a question guide, not a stem list, and why. OLD: "This guide follows the Australian year, season by season and month by month, with the questions worth putting to your florist for each one." NEW: "What grows well in a given month varies with the region, the grower and the year, so this guide does not give a fixed list of stems. It follows the Australian year, season by season and month by month, with the questions worth putting to your florist for each one, and links to our deeper month guides where we have them."

Put the one sourced flower answer in Key Takeaways. OLD: "- For a wedding abroad, the season follows the destination, so the florist there is the one to ask." NEW: "- Waratah is the clearest seasonal Australian wedding flower: its flowering is concentrated in spring.\n- For a wedding abroad, the season follows the destination, so the florist there is the one to ask." (keep the existing fact_104 tag on the new line)

Signpost the existing month and season guides near the top so a phone reader can jump. OLD: "Take them to your first meeting with your florist and ask each question for your month. Where we have a deeper guide for a month or season, it is linked." NEW: "Take them to your first meeting with your florist and ask each question for your month. Deeper guides: [spring](/in-season-flowers-for-your-spring-wedding), [winter](/7-blooms-you-need-in-your-2015-winter-wedding), [July](/7-in-season-wedding-flowers-for-the-july-bride), [August](/7-gorgeous-in-season-wedding-flowers-for-the-august-bride), [November](/7-in-season-flowers-for-the-november-bride) and [December](/8-in-season-flowers-for-december)."
